ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, with points $P$ and $Q$ located on sides $AC$ and $BC$ respectively, and $AP=CQ$. Lines $AQ$ and $BP$ intersect at point $O$. When $\angle CBP=45^\circ$ and $BQ=4\sqrt{6}$, what is the length of $OB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, construct $QH\perp BP$ at H, \\
since $\angle CBP=45^\circ$ and $QH\perp BP$, \\
it follows that $\angle PBQ=\angle BQH=45^\circ$, \\
hence $BH=HQ$, \\
given $BQ=4\sqrt{6}$, \\
it follows that $BH=HQ=4\sqrt{3}$, \\
since $\angle BOQ=60^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle AQH=30^\circ$, \\
therefore $HQ=\sqrt{3}OH$, \\
hence $OH=4$, \\
thus $OB=OH+BH=4\sqrt{3}+4=\boxed{4\sqrt{3}+4}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is an equilateral triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right; P is located on the right side AC, and Q is located on the base BC; segment BP connects from B to P, segment AQ connects from A to Q, and the two lines intersect at the interior point O. In the figure, Q is indeed on BC, therefore BQ and BC are collinear, and O is on BP and AQ. Then reason: Because △ABC is an equilateral triangle, AB=AC, and ∠BAP=∠ACQ=60°. It is also known that AP=CQ, so △ABP and △ACQ satisfy SAS corresponding congruence. From corresponding angles, ∠ABP=∠CAQ can be obtained. Combining with the relative directions of the two cevians in the figure, it can be known that the angle between BP and AQ is 60°, that is, ∠BOQ=60°. Since Q is on BC, BQ and BC are the same straight line; also O is on BP, so ∠OBQ=∠CBP=45°. Therefore, in △BOQ, ∠BOQ=60°, ∠OBQ=45°, so ∠BQO=75°. Use the sine rule: OB/BQ = sin75°/sin60°. It is known that BQ=4√6, so OB = 4√6 · sin75° / sin60°. Because sin75°=(√6+√2)/4, sin60°=√3/2, therefore OB = 4√6 · ((√6+√2)/4) · (2/√3) = 4√3+4. Final answer: OB=4√3+4.
